newsitem.title: VATICAN: Orthodox church won't attend Vatican celebration.
newsitem.headline: Orthodox church won't attend Vatican celebration.

text.p: The Orthodox church will not send a delegation to this weekend's annual Roman Catholic festival of Saints Peter and Paul for the first time in 21 years, a Vatican official said on Friday.

Chief Vatican spokesman Joaquin Navarro-Valls told reporters that the Ecumenical Patriarch of Istanbul, Bartholomew, would not be represented at Sunday's celebrations. He said the Orthodox church had given no reason for its decision.
The announcement came two weeks after the Russian Orthodox church pulled out of a proposed historic meeting between its Patriarch Alexiy and Pope John Paul.
Orthodox churches have voiced sharp criticism at a European Ecumenical Conference in Austria this week about the missionary work of the Catholic church in Eastern Europe.

If Patriarch Alexiy and the Polish pope had met, it would have been the first encounter of its kind since the Great Schism of 1054 which split western Christian churches looking to Rome and the eastern church based in Constantinople -- now Istanbul.
